identity.title: Saddle (perineal) sensory loss and reduced anal tone

technique.how: With a chaperone and consent, test light touch and pinprick over the perineum, perianal skin, buttocks and inner thighs (S2-S5) comparing sides and asking about numbness when wiping; then digital rectal examination assessing resting anal tone, voluntary squeeze, and perianal sensation/anal wink. Pair with a bladder scan for post-void residual.
technique.prerequisites: Chaperone, explanation and consent; document time of onset of bladder/bowel symptoms and bilateral leg symptoms.
technique.contraindications: Patient refusal; rectal exam may be deferred if imaging is already being obtained emergently, but perineal sensation should still be tested.

interpretation.positive_finding: New saddle sensory loss or reduced anal tone in a patient with back pain and bilateral leg or sphincter symptoms is a red flag that mandates emergency MRI; pooled red flags for MRI-confirmed cauda equina are more specific (0.62-0.88) than sensitive.
interpretation.negative_finding: Normal perineal sensation and anal tone do not exclude cauda equina compression - pooled sensitivities of individual red flags are only 0.19-0.43, and the diagnosis is often early or incomplete when sphincter signs are absent.
interpretation.pitfalls: Subjective perineal numbness is more sensitive than objective testing; anal tone is unreliable with prior anorectal surgery, chronic constipation or in the elderly. A large post-void residual (>500 mL) is the single most predictive bedside finding and should be checked with the exam.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: emergency MRI whole lumbosacral spine/urgent spinal surgical referral. Negative: does not exclude cauda equina; if suspicion persists (bilateral sciatica, retention) still image.

estimates.target_condition: MRI-confirmed cauda equina syndrome - individual red flags (reduced anal tone, saddle anaesthesia, urinary retention, incontinence, leg/back pain), pooled
estimates.population: Adults with suspected cauda equina syndrome; 7 studies, 569 participants
estimates.quote: The pooled sensitivity for the signs and symptoms ranged from 0.19 (95% CI 0.09 to 0.33) to 0.43 (95% CI 0.30 to 0.56)
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (Musculoskelet Sci Pract 2019;42:125); per-sign values in the paper's pooled-analysis table, not viewable

sources.citation: Dionne N, Adefolarin A, Kunzelman D, et al. What is the diagnostic accuracy of red flags related to cauda equina syndrome (CES), when compared to Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)? A systematic review. Musculoskelet Sci Pract. 2019;42:125-133.
Domen PM, Hofman PA, van Santbrink H, Weber WE. Predictive value of clinical characteristics in patients with suspected cauda equina syndrome. Eur J Neurol. 2009;16(3):416-419.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use normal anal tone or perineal sensation to defer imaging when bilateral sciatica, new urinary retention or incontinence is present; the exam is insensitive for early cauda equina.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Any new saddle sensory change, sphincter disturbance or retention with back pain is a surgical emergency: emergent MRI and spinal referral without waiting for full deficit.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No reliability data identified; anal tone assessment is subjective and examiner-dependent. Dionne 2019 rated included studies as generally low quality with two published corrigenda (PMIDs 31300389, 33722511) correcting pooled figures.

extraction_notes: The Dionne 2019 systematic review pooled saddle anaesthesia and reduced anal tone separately, but only the range across all red flags (sensitivity 0.19-0.43, specificity 0.62-0.88) is visible in the abstract; the per-sign table is behind a paywall and two corrigenda exist, so sign-specific sensitivity/specificity are set to null and the estimate is recorded as a range in the quote. Domen 2009 (abstract) found that individual signs including saddle/rectal findings did not differ significantly between MRI-positive and negative patients (n=58, 8 positive) and that >500 mL retention or >=2 of bilateral sciatica/subjective retention/rectal incontinence predicted compression (OR 48); no per-sign sens/spec in abstract. No open-access alternative with sign-specific numbers was found in 4 searches. NICE NG234 could not be retrieved and is not cited.
